transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir from Redwood, AE. Elena our solutions engineer is here, also Jordan from success. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Maya: Good thanks, excited to see this — we kicked off the brief earlier.
[00:12] Liam: Hey all, Liam here. Quick note, we're coming off an Elastic+FAISS proto and curious about accuracy uplift and operational cost.
[00:20] Elena: Great, we'll walk through hosted embeddings and the rerank endpoint — two-stage flow, then Console demo of the Optimize suggestions. I'll try to keep the deep kernel stuff light but I can dive deeper if you want.
[00:28] Priya: Quick infra context — we're on GCP, VPC peering concerns, SAML for SSO, need audit logs and KMS for keys.
[00:35] Samir: Perfect, we'll cover security items and share the SOC2 pack after. For this session I'll demo an end-to-end hosted API flow: embeddings generation, vector index integration and our reranker call that takes candidate doc ids+scores and returns re-ranked results.
[00:48] Elena: Alright jumping in — first slide is embeddings. Redwood supports host-side generation or you can bring your own vectors. Hosted embeddings are available via the /embeddings endpoint, typical dims 768 to 2048 depending on model. For product search we often recommend the 1536-ish profile for balance.
[01:10] Liam: When you say 1536-ish, is that a Red- model or open model? And what's the throughput?
[01:18] Elena: Good Q. We have a catalog with curated open models and some Redwood-verified variants. Throughput depends on instance type and batching — hosted can do ~600 qps on a dedicated pool with batching, but on shared hosted tiers it's more like 60-120 qps. There's also continuous batching and prefix caching to reduce unit token cost.
[01:35] Noah: Is prefix cache that the KV cache you mentioned earlier?
[01:38] Elena: Yeah KV cache — sorry sometimes the transcript spells it K V cash — it's the key-value decoder cache that speeds up autoregressive calls and can be used for prompt caching. For embeddings specifically we do vector cache heuristics when identical inputs are seen.
[01:53] Maya: Walk me through the reranker. We currently do coarse faiss search -> re-rank with a cross-encoder. How does Redwood slot in?
[02:02] Elena: Our hosted flow mirrors that. You run your ANN search (we don't force your index choice — FAISS, HNSW, Pinecone etc). Then you call Redwood's /rerank endpoint with the query, candidate ids and candidate text, optionally candidate embeddings. The reranker will call a cross-encoder style model and return final scores and structured metadata. The nice bit is you can do hybrid: use the hosted embedding generation to standardize dimensions and then store vectors in your own index.
[02:26] Liam: Any limit on candidate count? We typically pass 100 but sometimes need 200 for recall.
[02:31] Elena: Current hosted rerank soft limit is 200 candidates per request for latency considerations. For large jobs we recommend a two-pass cascade — quick scorer followed by the heavy cross-encoder on the top N.
[02:44] Samir: I'll show the Console now. Elena will run a live rerank on their sample data — small demo dataset we prepped.
[02:51] Elena: Switching to the Console — this is our per-model dashboard, you can select the model variant and preview embeddings. Over on the right we have auto-suggested Optimize configs: batching window, quantization profile (int8 or q4 variants), and caching policies.
[03:12] Priya: On quantization, curious about accuracy loss tradeoffs. If we go q4 or int8 for the reranker model what do we see?
[03:20] Elena: Usually q4 gives ~1-2% quality delta on rerank tasks versus full-fp16, int8 can be 2-4% depending on model and prompt. The Console includes a quick eval harness — you can run a prompt set and see metric deltas side-by-side. It's not perfect but gives a directional signal.
[03:38] Maya: Can we see the eval now? Even a couple examples?
[03:42] Elena: Yep, loading a small eval of 50 queries — pulling in their product descriptions. Running hosted rerank with our recommended candidate set of 50 and model variant redwood-cross-1536-q4.
[03:56] [04:00] Elena: (typing) — okay results came back — P@1 improved from 0.62 baseline to 0.73 on this sample. Latency median was 120ms for rerank only when using q4 on a dedicated pool.
[04:14] Liam: 120ms — that's rerank latency alone? Do you include roundtrip to our index?
[04:19] Elena: This is just the model inference time. If you host the index externally you'll add network+ANN query time. For hosted index options we can co-locate in the same region to keep p50+p95 low.
[04:30] Maya: What about cost estimates? We saw a vendor that charged per-candidate which got expensive.
[04:35] Samir: Redwood pricing for hosted is per-embedding and per-token inference; rerank calls are charged by compute time + per-request overhead, not per-candidate. We can share a detailed pricing sheet in the follow-up. We'll include burst capacity notes and Dedicated capacity options if you need predictable throughput.
[04:51] Priya: Dedicated capacity — if we move to dedicated, do we still get Console and Optimize features?
[04:56] Elena: Yes, Dedicated retains the full Console and Optimize tooling. The only difference is capacity isolation and SLA-backed latency. Private deployments are a different offering where the control plane can be customer-managed.
[05:08] Noah: Security quickfire: SOC2 type II, SAML/SSO ok, do you integrate with GCP KMS and can we have key control?
[05:17] Samir: Yes to SOC2; we integrate with customer KMS and support bring-your-own keys for Dedicated/Private. For hosted we offer KMS integrations and rotational keys, and we'll share the security FAQ and architecture notes.
[05:30] Liam: Any data retention or deletion guarantees for embeddings?
[05:34] Elena: Hosted default keeps logs for X days — we'll provide policy details. For compliance-sensitive customers we recommend Dedicated or Private where data does not persist beyond the customer-controlled VPC, and audit logs can be pulled into your SIEM.
[05:48] Maya: Can we run an A/B test using rollout policies? I want to compare current production ranker vs Redwood rerank in canary.
[05:56] Elena: Absolutely. Console supports rollout controls: canary at X% traffic, automatic fallback if latency or uplift thresholds not met, and per-route configurations. We can also integrate with your feature flagging.
[06:10] Samir: Let's run a quick live demo of the rerank call shape using Curl and then the SDK. Elena, would you run the sample query?
[06:18] Elena: Yep — showing the /v1/rerank POST body. You pass query text, candidates array [{id,text,score,embedding?}], and optional tuning params like reweight terms, or structured instructions for multi-attribute ranking.
[06:33] [06:40] Elena: (reads curl) curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"query":"black hiking jacket","candidates":[{"id":"p1","text":"..."}, {"id":"p2","text":"..."}]}' — response includes top_k, scores, and a reasons array if you enable explainability.
[06:58] Maya: Explainability — is that free? How detailed are the reasons?
[07:03] Elena: We include a lightweight reason vector: motif labels like "brand_match", "size_match", "freshness" — it's not a full Shapley analysis but helps triage. Deeper explainability is part of the enterprise add-on.
[07:18] Liam: On integration, we're worried about network hops and p95 spikes. What are common mitigations?
[07:25] Elena: A few: 1) co-locate index and Redwood region; 2) use prefix/KV caching for repeated queries; 3) tune batch windows for embeddings and rerank calls; 4) fallback model variants for degraded capacity. Optimize can make automated suggestions based on traffic pattern.
[07:43] Priya: Does Optimize show cost impact of each suggestion?
[07:47] Elena: Yes, the Console gives a token-level cost breakdown, expected cost delta for quantization choices, and projected throughput. We have a simulation mode to estimate monthly spend at your QPS.
[07:59] Noah: Any gotchas with client-side batching? We prefer to batch on the client.
[08:04] Elena: That works; Redwood's runtime supports continuous batching server-side too, so you can choose. If you batch on client then request sizes can grow and rerank candidate limits matter. Client batching is great for embeddings throughput.
[08:19] Samir: Let's talk pilot runway — what's needed to validate? Usually a 2-week pilot with 10k queries/day and a 50-100 query eval set. We run both baseline and Redwood rerank and measure P@1, CTR, and latency.
[08:34] Maya: Sounds right. We'll need to commit to providing product catalog slice + historical query logs.
[08:40] Priya: One more infra question — SAML and RBAC. We want SCIM provisioning and role-based scopes so only eng can hit the rerank endpoint for production.
[08:50] Samir: SCIM + SAML supported; roles map to token scopes and Console RBAC. We'll include the mapping doc.
[08:59] Elena: Quick technical deep-dive for Liam if you want: reranker uses attention optimizations and KV cache re-use when seeding from query context. For cross-encoder we support quantized kernels that shave inference time.
[09:15] Liam: Would like kernel-level perf numbers — p50/p95 on 16k tokens? That might be overkill but we have some long product descriptions.
[09:23] Elena: For long contexts we do sequence-length aware kernel selection. I'll pull some p50/p95 numbers for 1k and 4k sequences in the follow-up benchmark sheet.
[09:34] Maya: Can we set a budget cap to prevent runaway cost during the pilot?
[09:39] Samir: Yes, you can set per-route quotas and spending caps in Console. We'll also set alerting thresholds.
[09:48] Noah: Are there any limitations on language support? We have multi-lingual catalogue.
[09:52] Elena: We support many open models with multilingual embeddings; quality varies by language — Console eval will show per-lang deltas.
[10:03] [10:10] Elena: Running another quick rerank variant comparison — full FP16 cross vs q4 on same sample. Results show small drop for q4 but big cost/latency wins.
[10:22] Priya: What about caching invalidation — if product text updates frequently, how do we expire vector cache?
[10:27] Elena: Cache invalidation policies are configurable: TTL-based, event-triggered (webhook), or manual purge. For high churn data we recommend shorter TTLs and on-write purge hooks.
[10:40] Liam: Any third-party data sharing concerns? E.g., if we send candidate texts, do they persist?
[10:45] Samir: For hosted the default retention applies; for sensitive flows use Dedicated/Private. We'll share the retention policy.
[10:54] Maya: Can we do on-the-fly re-weighting like prefer newer inventory?
[10:58] Elena: Yes, you can pass structured signals and set feature weights in the rerank call or use dynamic rerank templates in Console.
[11:10] Samir: Ok we're ~11 minutes in — want to speed to the integration steps and pilot scope.
[11:16] Maya: Yes please.
[11:18] Elena: Integration options: 1) Hosted quickstart — SDK + sample script to call embeddings and rerank; 2) Dedicated pilot — reserved GPUs with throughput target; 3) Private — customer-managed control plane. For pilot we recommend Hosted quickstart first to validate quality, then move to Dedicated if throughput/cost requires.
[11:39] Priya: For the quickstart, what's the token auth flow? We use short-lived tokens mapped to roles.
[11:44] Samir: We support API keys and short-lived OAuth tokens tied to SAML assertions. We'll include recommended secret rotation cadence.
[11:54] Liam: How long does it take to onboard to Dedicated?
[11:57] Elena: Typically 4-6 weeks end-to-end depending on capacity and compliance needs. Hosted pilot can start in days.
[12:05] Maya: Okay let's plan the hosted pilot. Can we get an estimate table of expected monthly spend for 10k q/day with 100 candidates and rerank model q4?
[12:14] Samir: We'll provide that in the pricing breakdown.
[12:18] [12:20] Elena: Final quick demo — show SDK snippet in Python for embeddings + rerank, including how to attach candidate embeddings to avoid double compute.
[12:33] Elena: (reads) from redwood import Client; c = Client(api_key=...); embeddings = c.embeddings.create(input=queries); idx_results = call_your_ann(embeddings); rerank = c.rerank.create(query=q, candidates=top_candidates)
[12:49] Priya: If we attach candidate embeddings, do you charge for embedding generation on your side?
[12:54] Elena: If you supply embeddings we don't re-generate them, so you avoid that cost. But if you ask us to generate and store them via hosted we bill per-embedding.
[13:06] Maya: Any demo of Console alerts for regressions?
[13:10] Jordan: Yeah quick show — here in Console you can link an eval set and then set regression thresholds; we can trigger Slack/PagerDuty on regressions.
[13:23] Liam: I'm going to ask a bit of a nerdy question — how do you handle positional bias in rerank when product titles often repeat brand tokens?
[13:31] Elena: We have training-time heuristics and at inference you can pass reweighting rules; also the rerank model can accept features like position_in_initial_list to counteract bias.
[13:44] Maya: Great. Any compliance questionnaire we should fill for procurement?
[13:48] Samir: We'll send the security questionnaire link and the SOC2 report. Procurement can kick off while pilot runs.
[13:56] Priya: One more follow-up — do you support private endpoints inside our VPC for lower latency?
[14:01] Elena: Private deployment does that. For Hosted we provide VPC peering and regional co-location options. We'll include a network diagram.
[14:12] Maya: Let's recap next steps and owners.
[14:15] Samir: Recap: Samir send pricing/SLA and procurement pack; Elena share benchmark spreadsheet, SDK snippets and security FAQ; Customer to share eval dataset and infra constraints. Pilot kickoff tentative 2026-12-29.
[14:30] Maya: That timeline works.
[14:33] Liam: I'll prepare a small perf test harness and share it.
[14:37] Priya: I'll open a ticket with our infra team to gather VPC details.
[14:42] Samir: Awesome. Any final Qs?
[14:45] Noah: None from me.
[14:47] Maya: No, thanks — that was helpful.
[14:50] Samir: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up.
[14:55] Elena: Talk soon.
